By way of filing the instant criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the petitioners have prayed for the following relief:
"It is, therefore, most humbly and respectfully prayed, that this criminal misc.
petition under section 482 CRPC of the petitioners may very kindly be allowed and second and supplementary charge-sheet dated 21/2/2008 in fir no. 4. 445/07, PS Jawahar Nagar Sriganganagar, and second Criminal proceeding in criminal case no.
12/2012, pending before ACJM no. 2 Sriganganagar, may kindly be quashed and set aside."

Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that an FIR No.445/2007 dated 25.11.2007 was lodged against the petitioners [2024:RJ-JD:12498] (2 of 4) [CRLMP-1873/2019] for the offences under Section 8/21, 22, 29 of the NDPS Act.

The petitioners after facing regular trial have been Bajrang Lal Gupta vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:12498) on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44520567/
1 acquitted of the charges under the NDPS Act by the competent criminal court in Sessions Case No.8/2008 (State Vs. Bajrang Lal & Anr.) vide order dated 12.06.2019.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that the petitioners are again being tried on the same facts in connection with FIR No.445/2007 registered for offence under Section 420 IPC.
Learned counsel submitted that although the offences are different but the facts are the same.
The petitioners therefore, cannot be tried and convicted for the different offences, arising out of the same facts.
Reliance was placed on the judgment of Hon'ble the Supreme Court of India in the case of Kolla Veera Raghav Rao Vs. Gorantla Venkateswara Rao & Anr. reported in AIR 2011 Supreme Court 641.

sentences.text: Drawing attention of the court towards the impugned Supplementary Chargesheet dated 21.02.2008, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners have been booked for the said offence under section 420 IPC on the basis of one fake bill book allegedly submitted by co-accused Harish Gupta during the course of investigation.

Learned counsel contended that in the present matter, the said circumstance and the acts allegedly constituting the ingredients for offence under section 420 IPC along with the evidence available on the record of the case have already been sufficiently examined and dealt with by the learned Sessions Judge in the impugned order dated 12.06.2019.

On the strength of the above mentioned arguments, learned counsel thus implored the court that since the petitioners have [2024:RJ-JD:12498] (3 of 4) [CRLMP-1873/2019] already been acquitted by the competent criminal court on merit, the parallel proceedings against them on the same set of facts in the criminal case no. 12/2012, pending before ACJM no. 2 Sriganganagar, be quashed and set aside.
Learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the present misc. petition.
Heard learned counsel for the parties at Bar.

Upon a perusal of the impugned order dated 12.06.2019, this court finds that learned trial court while dealing with the statements of the seizure officer Bhoma Ram (PW 14) has taken on record that bill books, license etc. were allegedly seized at the instance of Harish Gupta as Ex.P. 38-41 and while appreciating this relevant evidence along with the other evidence available on record, have acquitted the petitioners of the said charge against him.

In the considered opinion of this court and peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, this court finds that though the charge for the offence under section 420 IPC was not dealt with by the learned Sessions Judge, however, since the evidence adduced against the accused-petitioners for the said offence have already been sufficiently dealt with by the learned trial court, in case if the trial for the offence under section 420 of IPC, pending against the accused-petitioners in criminal case no.
12/2012, before ACJM no. 2 Sriganganagar, is continued, it would gravely prejudice the case of the accused-petitioners.
In light of aforesaid discussion, the present criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed and the criminal proceedings in Cr.Case No.12/2012 pending in the court of ACJM No.2,
Sriganganagar are hereby quashed and set aside.
Stay application stands disposed of.
